chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Territory bands and musicians flowing to New York
summary: Hinton and Jackson say great musicians came from Louisville, Ohio, Kansas City, St. Louis and Atlanta to make New York the entertainment mecca.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So the thirties was very lucrative and hot for a musician beginning to play. The territorial bands were beginning to flow into New York, the territorial musicians --
Which is most interesting because in most historical jazz we only hear of the musicians coming from New Orleans, but we had these great territorial bands --

-- that played in their territory and people are beginning to recognize them and they begin to see, now that the Chicago era is over, everybody's beginning to flow to New York because this is the mecca now where -- entertainment mecca -- and they all began to flow into here.

So we get these great musicians that are perhaps unsung in the annals of famousness, and fame but were the backbone of all of the great orchestras, coming from all of these different cities and states, like you say Louisville, Kentucky, contributed.
That's right. Ohio contributed a lot.
Kansas City and St. Louis, Missouri.
And Atlanta, Georgia, had been there with Perry Bradford and all those guys who were doing it at the same time that that was happening in New Orleans.
-- than all these guys. So you name some more, just continue.
